BURSEVI:v10p385#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p385#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p385#3/r5.claim: Scales are either weighed deeds valued by God or literal balances; heaviness means predominance because truth is weighty and falsehood light, and the plural may magnify, assign a scale per person, or reflect many kinds of deeds.
BURSEVI:v10p385#3/r5.anchor: جمع الموزون وهو العمل الذي له وزن وخطر عند الله أو جمع ميزان وثقلها رجحانها

BURSEVI:v10p385#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p385#3/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
BURSEVI:v10p385#3/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas describes a balance with a tongue and two pans, in which deeds alone are weighed.
BURSEVI:v10p385#3/r6.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما ، إنه ميزان له لسان وكفتان

BURSEVI:v10p385#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p385#3/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p385#3/r7.claim: The deeds may be represented by their records to display justice and remove excuses, or deeds may take corresponding substantial forms, good beautiful and bad ugly, and then be weighed.
BURSEVI:v10p385#3/r7.anchor: قالوا توضع فيه صحف الأعمال إظهارا للمعدلة وقطعا للمعذرة أو تبرز الأعمال العرضية بصور جوهرية

BURSEVI:v10p385#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p385#3/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p385#3/r8.claim: Whoever's good deeds outweigh the rest will have a pleasing life; “pleased” may be attributed to the life because it causes satisfaction, or mean that the person is pleased with it.
BURSEVI:v10p385#3/r8.anchor: فمن ترجحت مقادير حسناته {فهو فى عيشة راضية}

QASHANI:101:6-10/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:101:6-10/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:101:6-10/r1.claim: Heavy scales are real sciences, psychic virtues, and heart and spirit perfections; their owner has a satisfied, true life in gardens of attributes above gardens of deeds.
QASHANI:101:6-10/r1.anchor: من العلوم الحقيقية والفضائل النفسانية والكمالات القلبية والروحانية

QASHANI:101:6-10/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:101:6-10/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:101:6-10/r4.claim: On the lesser-resurrection reading, people separate from bodies at death and rush toward the light-world in confusion shaped by scattered beliefs and desires, as bodily members disintegrate like fluffed wool.
QASHANI:101:6-10/r4.anchor: الموت يوم يكون الناس بفراقهم عن الأبدان وانبعاثهم من مراقدها

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p421/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p421/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p421/r4.claim: Only deeds will help: God weighs them in a just balance, granting eternal bliss when good deeds outweigh evil and Hell when the scales tip the other way.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p421/r4.anchor: God will set up the Balance of Justice in which all of man’s deeds will be weighed.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p424/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p424/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p424/r4.claim: Only deeds matter on that Day; good deeds that outweigh evil bring salvation, while the rest doom their bearers, and a special balance weighs human deeds.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p424/r4.anchor: meant only to weigh the deeds of men

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p425/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p425/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p425/r1.claim: The balance gives weight only to truth, meaning good deeds; the light-scaled lose because they denied God’s revelations.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p425/r1.anchor: On that day, the truth only will have weight.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p425/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p425/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p425/r2.claim: The relative singular man in the scale descriptions denotes a plural group.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p425/r2.anchor: as used in the verse above denotes plurality.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p425/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p425/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p425/r3.claim: Dwelling in bliss means receiving not only whatever one wishes but also what one could never imagine.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p425/r3.anchor: not only will they be granted whatever they wish for but also what they cannot even imagine.

QUSHAYRI:v3p444/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p444/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p444/r8.claim: Those whose scales are heavy with good deeds will have a pleasing life; “pleasing” means made pleasing to them.
QUSHAYRI:v3p444/r8.anchor: من ثقلت موازينه بالخيرات فهو في عيشة راضية ؛ أي مرضية

QUSHAYRI:v3p444/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p444/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p444/r9.claim: One account says deeds are weighed through the weighing of their written records.
QUSHAYRI:v3p444/r9.anchor: ووزن الأعمال يومئذ يكون بوزن الصحف

QUSHAYRI:v3p444/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p444/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p444/r10.claim: Another account says a substance will be created for each component of a person's acts, and those substances will be weighed as the deeds' measure.
QUSHAYRI:v3p444/r10.anchor: ويقال : يخلق بدل كل جزء من أفعاله جوهرا

SULAMI:v2p416/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p416/r1.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v2p416/r1.claim: In answer to whether deeds make scales heavy, the Wāsiṭī says God makes them heavy or light as He wills; a report says the scales are in God's hand, who raises and lowers people according to pre-eternal decree.
SULAMI:v2p416/r1.anchor: وقيل للواسطي رحمه الله : هل يجوز أن تثقل الموازين بأعمالنا فإن لو جاز ذلك لا من كل من كثرت أعماله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p533/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p533/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p533/r3.claim: The author points back to earlier discussion of the weighing and to the description of a pleasing life in Sūrat al-Ḥāqqa.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p533/r3.anchor: وتقدم الكلام في الموازين وثقلها وخفتها في الأعراف، وعيشة راضية في الحاقة.

FARRA:v3p286/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p286/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p286/r4.claim: Mawāzīn can mean weights as well as scales, as in asking whether a coin matches another coin's weight.
FARRA:v3p286/r4.anchor: ووزنه، والعرب تقول: هل لك في درهم بميزان درهمك ووزن درهمك،

FARRA:v3p286/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p286/r5.speaker: شاعر
FARRA:v3p286/r5.claim: A poet uses mīzānah for the measure or weight of an opponent's words, attesting the sense of weighing.
FARRA:v3p286/r5.anchor: وقال الشاعر: قد كنت قبل لقائكم ذا مرة ... عندي لكل مخاصم ميزانه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#2/r1.claim: The passage briefly divides people into two groups and introduces each group's particular fate after describing conditions common to all.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#2/r1.anchor: بيان اجمالي لتحزب الناس حزبين وتنبيه على كيفية الاحوال الخاصة بكل نهما اثر بيان الاحوال

ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#2/r2.claim: The verse indicates the weighing of deeds, which must be believed literally; denying it does not make a person an unbeliever.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#2/r2.anchor: وهذا اشارة إلى وزن الاعمال وهو مما يجب الايمان به حقيقة ولايكفر منكره

ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#2/r3.claim: The weighing occurs after the records fly and are taken in right and left hands, and after questioning and reckoning, as al-Wāḥidī and others say.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#2/r3.anchor: ويكون بعد تطاير الصحف وأخذها بالايمان والشمائل وبعد السؤال والحساب كما ذكره الواحدي

ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#2/r4.claim: The balance is a real scale with a tongue and two pans, as broad as the heavens and earth; its modality is unknown.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#2/r4.anchor: بميزان له لسان وكفتان كاطباق السموات والأرض والله تعالى أعلم بما هيته

ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس، الحسن البصري
ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#2/r5.claim: The physical balance view is transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī and attributed to many exegetes.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#2/r5.anchor: وقد روى القول به عن ابن عباس والحسن البصري وعزاه في شرح المقاصد لكثير من المفسرين

ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#2/r6.claim: Some say the scale is between Paradise and Hell, hangs from the Throne, and is held by Gabriel while Michael is entrusted with it.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#2/r6.anchor: وكانه بين الجنة والنار كما في نوادر الاصول وذكر يتقبل به العرش أخذ جبريل

ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#2/r7.claim: The better-known and sounder view is one balance for all nations and all deeds.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#2/r7.anchor: والاشهر الاصح انه ميزان واحد كما ذكرنا لجميع الامم ولجميع الاعمال

ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#2/r8.claim: Mawāzīn is plural of mīzān, originally mawzān; proposed reasons include magnification, its component parts, or multiple instances by different considerations.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#2/r8.anchor: فقوله تعالى موازينه وهو جمع ميزان وأصله موزان بالواو لكن قلبت ياء

ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#3/r1.speaker: الرازي
ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#3/r1.claim: Al-Razi is reported to have claimed that a Prophetic report supports the weighing of deeds.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#3/r1.anchor: وزعم الرازي على مانقل عنه أن فيه حديثا مرفوعا

ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#3/r2.speaker: آخرون
ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#3/r2.claim: Some say deeds themselves are weighed after righteous and sinful acts take luminous or dark forms, placed in corresponding pans; their weight reflects divine grace and justice.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#3/r2.anchor: وقال آخرون يوزن نفس الاعمال فتصور الصالحة بصور حسنة نورانية ثم تطرح في كفة النور

ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#3/r3.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#3/r3.claim: Others say God creates bodies equal in number to deeds, without transforming the deeds; they claim a transmitted report supports this.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#3/r3.anchor: وقد ذهب بعضهم إلى أن الله تعالى يخلق أجساما على عدد تلك الاعمال من غير قلب لها

ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#3/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#3/r4.claim: The apparent sense compares weight and lightness to worldly gravity: heavy deeds descend before rising to Illiyyin, and light ones rise before falling to Sijjin; al-Qurtubi states this explicitly.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#3/r4.anchor: والظاهر ان الثقل والخفة مثلها في الدنيا فما ثقل نزل

ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#3/r5.speaker: بعض المتأخرين
ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#3/r5.claim: Some later scholars reverse worldly behavior: a believer's good deeds rise when they outweigh, while a disbeliever's pan is heavy because its other pan lacks good deeds; the author's cited proof is questionable.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#3/r5.anchor: وقال بعض المتأخرين هما على خلاف مافي الدنيا وأن عمل المؤمن اذا رجح صعد وثقلت سيآته

ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#3/r6.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#3/r6.claim: One account says all deeds are placed on the scales at once, with good deeds in a luminous right pan toward Paradise and sins in a dark pan toward Hell; God gives each person necessary knowledge of their relative weight.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#3/r6.anchor: وذكر بعضهم أن صفة الوزن أن يجعل جميع أعمال العباد في الميزان مرة واحدة الحسنات في كفة النور

ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#3/r7.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#3/r7.claim: A related account says a luminous column from the good-deed pan covering the other pan signals preponderance, while a dark column from the sin pan covering the good pan signals lightness.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#3/r7.anchor: وقيل نحوه الا ان علامة الرجحان عمود من نور يثور من كفة الحسنات

ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#3/r8.speaker: القرطبي
ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#3/r8.claim: Al-Qurtubi says not everyone is weighed: some enter Paradise without reckoning, while sinners may instead be identified by their marks and seized; weighing remains for those God wills.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#3/r8.anchor: قال القرطبي لايكون في حق كل أحد لما في الحديث الصحيح فيقال يامحمد أدخل الجنة من أمتك من لاحساب عليهم

ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#3/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#3/r9.speaker: القاضي منذر بن سعيد البلوطي
ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#3/r9.claim: Al-Qadi Mundhir ibn Sa'id al-Baluti says the patient are not weighed; their reward is poured out to them.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#3/r9.anchor: وذكر القاضي منذر بن سعيد البلوطي أن أهل الصبر لاتوزن أعمالهم وانما يصب لهم الأجر صبا

ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#3/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#3/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#3/r10.claim: The hypocrite apparently falls under the disbeliever, but the author holds that everyone's deeds are weighed, based on the plain sense of many verses and reports; the intended weighing is beneficial weighing.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#3/r10.anchor: والظاهر أنه يدرج المنافق في الكافر والحق أن أعمالهم مطلقا توزن لظواهر الآيات والاحاديث الكثيرة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#3/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#3/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#3/r11.claim: Believing and unbelieving jinn are subject to weighing just like humans; the distinctions described concern only those whose deeds are weighed.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#3/r11.anchor: والصحيح ان الجن مؤمنهم وكافرهم كالانس في هذا الشأن

ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#3/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#3/r12.speaker: المعتزلة
ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#3/r12.claim: The Mu'tazilites deny that the scales are literal.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#3/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#3/r13.speaker: مجاهد والضحاك والاعمش
ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#3/r13.claim: Mujahid, al-Dahhak, and al-A'mash say deeds are accidents that cannot be weighed; the scales instead represent just judgment.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#3/r13.anchor: منهم مجاهد والضحاك والاعمش قالوا ان الاعمال أعراض ان أمكن بقاؤها لايمكن وزنها فالوزن عبارة عن القضاء السوي والحكم العادل

ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#3/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#3/r14.speaker: الفراء
ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#3/r14.claim: Al-Farra allows mawazin to mean weighed things: deeds that have weight and standing with God; their heaviness means their measure outweighs.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p221#3/r14.anchor: وجوزوا فيما هنا أن تكون الموازين جمع موزون وهو العمل الذي له وزن وخطر عند الله تعالى

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p511#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p511#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p511#2/r6.claim: Heavy scales mean that a person's good deeds outweigh the bad.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p511#2/r6.anchor: {فأما من ثقلت موازينه} رجحت حسناته [على سيئاته] (5) .

BAYDAWI-FULL:101:1-11/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:101:1-11/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:101:1-11/r4.claim: Heavy scales mean the total weight of kinds of good deeds prevails.
BAYDAWI-FULL:101:1-11/r4.anchor: { فأما من ثقلت موزينه } بأن ترجحت مقادير أنواع حسناته

BIQAI-FULL:v8p514/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p514/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p514/r3.claim: Heavy scales are the weight of good deeds: the scales are plural because good deeds have many kinds, and either the deeds themselves or their records are weighed.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p514/r3.anchor: ولما كانت الموزونات كثيرة الأنواع جدا , جمع الميزان باعتبارها

BIQAI-FULL:v8p514/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p514/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p514/r4.claim: A person whose good deeds outweigh falsehood enters a life of lasting, consistent pleasure; rāḍiya can mean either possessing satisfaction or being pleasing.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p514/r4.anchor: { فهو } بسبب رجحان حسناته { في عيشة } أي حياة تتقلب فيها

NAHHAS:v5p280/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p280/r7.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p280/r7.claim: Man is the subject and the clause that follows is its predicate.
NAHHAS:v5p280/r7.anchor: من في موضع رفع بالابتداء والجملة الخبر

NAHHAS:v5p280/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p280/r8.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v5p280/r8.claim: He interprets the scales as the person's weight.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p512/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p512/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p512/r6.claim: The two outcomes detail the general human condition at the gathering, dividing people into a good and a frightening state.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p512/r6.anchor: تفصيل لما في قوله : { يوم يكون الناس كالفراش المبثوث } ( القارعة : 4 )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p512/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p512/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p512/r7.claim: Heavy scales figuratively signal God's approval through abundant good deeds; Arabic uses weight for merit and honor, so the deeds need not be named explicitly.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p512/r7.anchor: وثقل الموازين كناية عن كونه بمحل الرضى من الله تعالى لكثرة حسناته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p512/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p512/r8.speaker: ابن العربي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p512/r8.claim: Ibn al-Arabi says no sound hadith establishes the scale's physical nature; the point is that no deed is lost, which God can realize by an instrument, angels, or another means.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p512/r8.anchor: قال ابن العربي في ( العواصم ) : لم يرد حديث صحيح في الميزان

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p468#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p468#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p468#2/r6.claim: A person whose good deeds outweigh their bad deeds will have a pleasing life in Paradise.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p468#2/r6.anchor: رجحت حسناته على سيئاته، {فهو في عيشة راضية} يعني: في الجنة

KASHSHAF:101:6/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:101:6/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:101:6/r1.claim: Mawāzīn may be the plural of 'weighed thing,' meaning deeds of weight and worth before God, or a plural of 'scale.'
KASHSHAF:101:6/r1.anchor: جمع موزون ،   وهو العمل الذي له وزن وخطر عند الله

KASHSHAF:101:6/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:101:6/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:101:6/r2.claim: Heavy scales mean that the good deeds outweigh the bad.
KASHSHAF:101:6/r2.anchor: وثقلها : رجحانها . ومنه حديث أبي بكر

KASHSHAF:101:6/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:101:6/r3.speaker: أبو بكر
KASHSHAF:101:6/r3.claim: In advice to Umar, Abu Bakr says truth-followers gain heavy scales and falsehood-followers light ones, as each scale appropriately holds only good deeds or only sins.
KASHSHAF:101:6/r3.anchor: في وصيته له : «وإنما ثقلت موازين من ثقلت موازينهم يوم القيامة باتباعهم الحق

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p327#2/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p327#2/r12.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p327#2/r12.claim: Al-Hasan says the scales are a real balance with two pans for weighing good and bad deeds; Abu Bakr says a scale holding only truth deserves to be heavy.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p327#2/r12.anchor: أحدها : أنه ميزان ذو كفتين توزن به الحسنات والسيئات , قاله الحسن

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p327#2/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p327#2/r13.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p327#2/r13.claim: Mujahid says the scales mean the account, as illustrated by calling the human tongue their measure and by a poem about the measure.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p328/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p328/r1.speaker: عبد العزيز بن يحيى
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p328/r1.claim: Abd al-Aziz ibn Yahya says the scales are proofs and arguments, citing the same poem as evidence.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p328/r1.anchor: الثالث : أن الموازين الحجج والدلائل , قاله عبد العزيز بن يحيى , واستشهد فيه بالشعر المتقدم .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p328/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p328/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p328/r2.claim: Mawardi says موازين may be a plural of ميزان, or a plural meaning weighed things.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p328/r2.anchor: وفي الموازين وجهان : أحدهما : جمع ميزان . الثاني : أنه جمع موزون .

MUQATIL:101:1-6/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:101:1-6/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:101:1-6/r4.claim: Heavy scales belong to those whose good deeds outweigh their evil deeds.
MUQATIL:101:1-6/r4.anchor: { فأما من ثقلت موازينه } [آية: 6] يقول: من رجحت موازينه بحسناته

NASAFI-FULL:v4p354#6/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p354#6/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p354#6/r1.claim: Heavy scales may mean that deeds are weighty through adherence to the truth; mawāzīn may be the plural of a weighed deed valued by God.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p354#6/r1.anchor: باتباعهم الحق وهى جمع موزون وهو العمل الذى له وزن وخطر عند الله

NASAFI-FULL:v4p354#6/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p354#6/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p354#6/r2.claim: Alternatively, mawāzīn means actual scales, whose heaviness is their balance tipping in favor of good deeds.

QURTUBI:101:6/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:101:6/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI:101:6/r1.claim: The author refers readers to earlier discussions of the balance in al-Aʿrāf, al-Kahf, and al-Anbiyāʾ, and in his book al-Tadhkira.

QURTUBI:101:6/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:101:6/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI:101:6/r2.claim: The balance has a pan and a tongue, and weighs written records of good and bad deeds.
QURTUBI:101:6/r2.anchor: وأن له كفة ولسانا توزن فيه الصحف المكتوب فيها الحسانات والسيئات

QURTUBI:101:6/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:101:6/r3.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:101:6/r3.claim: One view says a single balance held by Gabriel weighs human deeds, expressed in the plural; a poem also uses plural balances.
QURTUBI:101:6/r3.anchor: ثم قيل : إنه ميزان واحد بيد جبريل يزن أعمال بني آدم

QURTUBI:101:6/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:101:6/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI:101:6/r4.claim: The author cites poetic usage of the plural balances for separate events.
QURTUBI:101:6/r4.anchor:
كما قال :
فلكل حادثةٍ لها مِيزَانُ

QURTUBI:101:6/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:101:6/r5.speaker: عبد العزيز بن يحيى
QURTUBI:101:6/r5.claim: Abd al-Aziz ibn Yahya says the balances are proofs and arguments, citing a poet who calls the argument of each disputant his balance.
QURTUBI:101:6/r5.anchor: الحجج والدلائل ، قاله عبد العزيز بن يحيى

QUTB-ZILAL:101:6/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:101:6/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:101:6/r1.claim: Heavy scales mean deeds or values that count in God’s judgment and assessment.
QUTB-ZILAL:101:6/r1.anchor: وثقل الموازين وخفتها تفيدنا : قيما لها عند الله اعتبار

QUTB-ZILAL:101:6/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:101:6/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:101:6/r2.claim: He cautions that rational or verbal disputes over how the scales work violate the Qur’an’s felt meaning and distract from genuine concern for the Qur’an and Islam.
QUTB-ZILAL:101:6/r2.anchor: فالدخول في جدل عقلي ولفظي حول هذه التعبيرات هو جفاء للحس القرآني

RAZI-FULL:v32p70/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p70/r1.speaker: الفراء
RAZI-FULL:v32p70/r1.claim: Al-Farraʾ takes موازين as weighed deeds, meaning actions that have weight and consequence with God.
RAZI-FULL:v32p70/r1.anchor: أحدهما : أنه جمع موزون وهو العمل الذي له وزن وخطر

RAZI-FULL:v32p70/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p70/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v32p70/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas takes موازين as scales with a tongue and two pans; good deeds appear beautiful and outweigh, while the unbeliever's ugly deeds are light.
RAZI-FULL:v32p70/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس : الميزان له لسان وكفتان

RAZI-FULL:v32p70/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p70/r3.speaker: الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v32p70/r3.claim: Al-Hasan says the scale has two pans but its nature is not described.
RAZI-FULL:v32p70/r3.anchor: وقال الحسن : في الميزان له كفتان ولا يوصف

RAZI-FULL:v32p70/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p70/r4.speaker: المتكلمون
RAZI-FULL:v32p70/r4.claim: Theologians say past good and bad acts cannot themselves be weighed; instead, written records, light and darkness, or beautiful and ugly forms of records display their weight.
RAZI-FULL:v32p70/r4.anchor: قال المتكلمون : إن نفس الحسنات والسيئات لا يصح وزنهما

RAZI-FULL:v32p70/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p70/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p70/r5.claim: The weighing publicly reveals the righteous person's state and increases joy, while exposing the evildoer to humiliation before all creatures.
RAZI-FULL:v32p70/r5.anchor: وتكون الفائدة في ذلك ظهور حال صاحب الحسنات في الجمع العظيم فيزداد سرورا

STUDYQURAN:101:intro/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:101:intro/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:101:intro/r3.claim: The final six verses contrast the recompense of those whose scales are heavy with good deeds and those whose scales are light.
STUDYQURAN:101:intro/r3.anchor: The last six verses (vv. 6–11) contrast the recompense

STUDYQURAN:101:6/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:101:6/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:101:6/r1.claim: The scales are heavy with good deeds.
STUDYQURAN:101:6/r1.anchor: Scales are heavy with good deeds.

STUDYQURAN:101:6/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:101:6/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:101:6/r2.claim: Mawāzīn is plural of mīzān: the Qur'an uses balance for revelation and revealed just order, but scales for weighing deeds at Resurrection.
STUDYQURAN:101:6/r2.anchor: is employed in the Quran to indicate revelation itself

STUDYQURAN:101:6/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:101:6/r3.speaker: Āl
STUDYQURAN:101:6/r3.claim: Although the plural suggests each person's experience of weighing, most say one scale weighs all deeds.
STUDYQURAN:101:6/r3.anchor: The plural, scales, speaks to how each individual will experience the weighing of his or her deeds, but according to most, it is in fact one scale

STUDYQURAN:101:6/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:101:6/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:101:6/r4.claim: Good and evil deeds are unequal; good deeds remove evil deeds, and a good deed earns tenfold while an evil deed is repaid only in kind.
STUDYQURAN:101:6/r4.anchor: From a Quranic perspective, the good deed and the evil deed are not equal (41:34), and good deeds remove those that are evil (11:114).

STUDYQURAN:101:6/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:101:6/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:101:6/r5.claim: A hadith says nothing placed in the Balance weighs more heavily than good character.
STUDYQURAN:101:6/r5.anchor: There is nothing placed in the Balance that is heavier than goodness of character

STUDYQURAN:101:6/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:101:6/r6.speaker: the Prophet
STUDYQURAN:101:6/r6.claim: A hadith says deeds are judged according to intentions, and each person receives what was intended.
STUDYQURAN:101:6/r6.anchor: another ḥadīth states, “Deeds are only in accord with their intentions. And every person has only what he intended.”

STUDYQURAN:101:6/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:101:6/r7.speaker: the Prophet
STUDYQURAN:101:6/r7.claim: A hadith says no one enters Paradise through deeds alone; when asked whether this included him, the Prophet said only God's mercy would shelter him.
STUDYQURAN:101:6/r7.anchor: As a ḥadīth states, “None of you will enter Paradise by his deeds.” Someone asked, “Not even you, O Messenger of God?”

TAB:101:6/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:101:6/r1.speaker: author
TAB:101:6/r1.claim: The verse means those whose good deeds weigh heavily; Arabic can use weight or a balance to mean something aligned or equivalent.
TAB:101:6/r1.anchor: فأما من ثقُلَت موازين حسناته ،   يعني بالموازين :  الوزن ،   والعرب تقول :  لك عندي درهم بميزان درهمك ،   ووزن درهمك

TAB:101:6/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:101:6/r2.speaker: author
TAB:101:6/r2.claim: A cited poet uses ميزانه for a disputant's argument or speech that answers and refutes the opponent.
TAB:101:6/r2.anchor: يعني بقوله :  «لكلّ مخاصم ميزانه » :  كلامه ،   وما ينقض عليه حجته

TAB:101:6/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:101:6/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB:101:6/r3.claim: Mujāhid says there is no literal scale here; the wording is a parable.
TAB:101:6/r3.anchor: وكان مجاهد يقول :  ليس ميزان ،   إنما هو مثل ضرب

ASAD-NOTES:101:intro/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:101:intro/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:101:intro/r1.claim: This is an early Meccan surah, probably revealed after At-Tin (surah 95).
ASAD-NOTES:101:intro/r1.anchor: An early Meccan surah, most probably revealed after surah 95 (At-Tin)

TABATABAI:101:1-9/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:101:1-9/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:101:1-9/r1.claim: The Meccan surah warns and gives glad tidings about resurrection, with warning as its dominant tone.
TABATABAI:101:1-9/r1.anchor: بيان إنذار وتبشير بالقيامة يغلب فيه جانب الانذار، والسورة مكية

TABATABAI:101:1-9/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:101:1-9/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:101:1-9/r10.claim: The scale weighs deeds: faith and obedience have weight and standing with God, while disbelief and sins do not; the heavy deeds bring felicity and the light ones misery.
TABATABAI:101:1-9/r10.anchor: الأعمال منها ما هو ثقيل في الميزان وهو ما له قدر ومنزلة عند الله وهو الإيمان وأنواع الطاعات

TABATABAI:101:1-9/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:101:1-9/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:101:1-9/r11.claim: The explanation of the scale has already been discussed in commentary on earlier surahs.
TABATABAI:101:1-9/r11.anchor: وقد تقدم البحث عن معنى الميزان في تفسير السور السابقة

TABRISI:101:5-11/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:101:5-11/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:101:5-11/r2.claim: Heavy scales mean abundant good deeds and many acts of goodness.

THALABI:v10p274#3/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p274#3/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p274#3/r4.claim: Those whose scales weigh heavily have a pleasing, well-pleased-with-it life in Paradise.
THALABI:v10p274#3/r4.anchor: فهو في عيشة راضية مرضية في الجنة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p264/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p264/r4.speaker: مقاتل والكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p264/r4.claim: Muqatil and al-Kalbi say that the person whose scales are heavy has good deeds that outweigh.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p264/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p264/r8.speaker: أبو بكر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p264/r8.claim: Abu Bakr says their scales are heavy because they follow truth, which weighs heavily; a balance containing only truth should be heavy, while one holding falsehood should be light.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p264/r8.anchor: قال أبو بكر: إنما ثقلت موازينهم باتباعهم الحق، وثقلت (¬1) عليهم. وحق لميزان لا يوضع فيه إلا الحق أن يكون ثقيلا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p264/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p264/r9.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p264/r9.claim: Muqatil similarly says the truth is heavy and falsehood is light.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p264/r9.anchor: ونحو هذا ذكر مقاتل، وقال: لأن الحق ثقيل، والباطل خفيف

WAHIDI-QT:101:6/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:101:6/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:101:6/r1.claim: His scales are heavy with good deeds.

ELMALILI:101:6-7/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:101:6-7/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:101:6-7/r1.claim: Mawāzīn may be the plural of mīzān, derived from wazn with the expected sound change, or the plural of mawzūn.
ELMALILI:101:6-7/r1.anchor: “vezn”den vâv ile “mivzân”dır. Vâv sâkin mâkabli meksur olduğu için

ELMALILI:101:6-7/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:101:6-7/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:101:6-7/r2.claim: A scale literally measures weight, but by metaphor it can compare intangible relations such as justice and rights, or balance an account.
ELMALILI:101:6-7/r2.anchor: Mâlum ki “mîzan” tartı âleti, eşyânın veznini, yani sıklet nisbetini ölçmeye mahsus olan terazi demektir.

ELMALILI:101:6-7/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:101:6-7/r3.speaker: Ferrâ
ELMALILI:101:6-7/r3.claim: Ferrā takes mawāzīn as the plural of mawzūn: deeds that possess weight and value before God.
ELMALILI:101:6-7/r3.anchor: Ferrâ buna kāil olmuş ve demiştir ki: ‘Bunun nazîri «bende senin dirheminin mîzânı

ELMALILI:101:6-7/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:101:6-7/r4.speaker: İbn Abbas
ELMALILI:101:6-7/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas describes a scale with one tongue and two pans: the obedient person's good deeds appear beautiful and outweigh, while the unbeliever's ugly sins are light.
ELMALILI:101:6-7/r4.anchor: İbn Abbas demiştir ki: ‘Mîzânın bir dili ve iki kefesi vardır. Onda ancak ameller vezn olunur.

ELMALILI:101:6-7/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:101:6-7/r5.speaker: Hasan
ELMALILI:101:6-7/r5.claim: Hasan reports that the scale has two pans, though their nature cannot be described.
ELMALILI:101:6-7/r5.anchor: Hasan’dan da ‘iki kefesi vardır, fakat tavsif olunamaz’ diye mervîdir.

ELMALILI:101:6-7/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:101:6-7/r6.speaker: Mütekellimîn
ELMALILI:101:6-7/r6.claim: The theologians offer several ways deeds can be weighed: their written records, light and darkness as signs, or deeds taking beautiful and ugly forms.
ELMALILI:101:6-7/r6.anchor: Mütekellimîn demişlerdir ki hasenât ve seyyiâtın kendileri husûsâ inkızâlarından sonra kābil-i vezn değildir.

ELMALILI:101:6-7/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:101:6-7/r7.speaker: Mücâhid, A‘meş ve Dahhâk
ELMALILI:101:6-7/r7.claim: They interpret weighing as sound judgment and just ruling; many later scholars prefer this because expired accidents cannot be physically weighed.
ELMALILI:101:6-7/r7.anchor: Mücâhid, A‘meş ve Dahhâk buna kāil olmuşlar. Müteahhirînden birçoğu da bunu ihtiyar eylemişler

ELMALILI:101:6-7/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:101:6-7/r8.speaker: Müteahhirînden birçokları
ELMALILI:101:6-7/r8.claim: They object that scales measure bodily heaviness, not the quantities of deeds that have ceased to exist as accidents.
ELMALILI:101:6-7/r8.anchor: Mîzan ile ancak ecsâmın sıkletleri mikdârı bilinebilir, a‘râzı münkazıye olan a‘mâlin mekādîri onunla nasıl vezn olunur?

ELMALILI:101:6-7/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:101:6-7/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:101:6-7/r9.claim: This objection denies only corporeal weighing, not every real measure; justice requires a true standard between things, as the revealed Book and Balance show.
ELMALILI:101:6-7/r9.anchor: Lâkin şunu itiraf etmek lâzım gelir ki bunun mânası mutlak mîzan ve vezni inkâr değil

ELMALILI:101:6-7/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:101:6-7/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:101:6-7/r10.claim: The scales of justice established for Resurrection are a true law that fully manifests justice and resolves the upheaval of the gathering.
ELMALILI:101:6-7/r10.anchor: kıyamet günü için konulacak olan adalet mîzanları da aynı mânada olarak adaleti hakkıyla tecellî ettirmek üzere vaz‘olunacak hak kanunu olmalıdır

ELMALILI:101:6-7/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:101:6-7/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:101:6-7/r11.claim: Measurement can apply to accidents as well as bodies; heat and cold, for example, are weighed by measures suited to them.
ELMALILI:101:6-7/r11.anchor: Bu mâna ile mîzânın tatbîki ise yalnız ecsâmda değil, a‘râzda da cereyan eder.

ELMALILI:101:6-7/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:101:6-7/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:101:6-7/r12.claim: True weighing on that Day must have an appropriate scale, but its nature exceeds human understanding; belief in its truth is required, while belief in a detailed mechanism is not.
ELMALILI:101:6-7/r12.anchor: amellerin hakikatine göre bunun mâhiyet ve keyfiyetinin tâyin ve tavsîfi bizim idrak ve dirayetimizin ihâtası sahasından uzaktır.

ELMALILI:101:6-7/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:101:6-7/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:101:6-7/r13.claim: Corporeal weighing remains conceivable because deeds have bodily effects and consequences of reward or punishment that take form in the afterlife.
ELMALILI:101:6-7/r13.anchor: eserleri itibariyle cismânî haysiyet ve kıymetleri hâiz olduklarında da şüphe yoktur.

ELMALILI:101:6-7/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:101:6-7/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:101:6-7/r14.claim: The reported weighing of beautiful and ugly deed-forms, records, or their light and darkness can all describe weighing through a deed's effects.
ELMALILI:101:6-7/r14.anchor: defter-i a‘mâlin vezni veya alâmetleri olan nûr ve zulmetin vezni hakkındaki kaviller veya rivayetler de yine âsâr itibariyle vezin mânasına râci‘olur.

ELMALILI:101:6-7/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:101:6-7/r15.speaker: Âlûsî
ELMALILI:101:6-7/r15.claim: Alusi says the verse indicates the weighing of deeds and requires literal belief in it, but one who denies it is not declared an unbeliever.
ELMALILI:101:6-7/r15.anchor: Âlûsî demiştir ki: “Bu âyet vezn-i a‘mâle işarettir ve buna hakikat olarak iman vâcibdir.

ELMALILI:101:6-7/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:101:6-7/r16.speaker: Vâhidî ve daha başkaları
ELMALILI:101:6-7/r16.claim: The weighing occurs after the records fly and are given from the right or left, and after questioning and reckoning.
ELMALILI:101:6-7/r16.anchor: Vâhidî ve daha başkaları böyle zikretmişlerdir.

ELMALILI:101:6-7/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:101:6-7/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:101:6-7/r17.claim: The scale has one tongue and two pans like the layers of the heavens and earth, but God alone knows its nature; this is reported from Ibn Abbas and Hasan and assigned to most exegetes.
ELMALILI:101:6-7/r17.anchor: bir lisânı ve Arz u semâvâtın atbâkı gibi iki kefesi bulunan bir mîzan ile olacaktır ki mâhiyetini ancak Allah bilir.

ELMALILI:101:6-7/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:101:6-7/r18.speaker: Nevâdiru’l-Usûl
ELMALILI:101:6-7/r18.claim: The scale is located between Paradise and Hell.
ELMALILI:101:6-7/r18.anchor: göre mekânı da cennet ile nâr arasıdır.

ELMALILI:101:6-7/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:101:6-7/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:101:6-7/r19.claim: The stronger view is one scale for all communities and deeds; the plural may honor it, refer to its parts, or reflect conceptual multiplicity, while plural mawzūn needs no such interpretation.
ELMALILI:101:6-7/r19.anchor: Eşher ve esah olan da bu, cemî‘-i ümem ve cemî‘-i a‘mâl için zikrolunduğu

ELMALILI:101:6-7/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:101:6-7/r20.speaker: author
ELMALILI:101:6-7/r20.claim: If mawāzīn means weighed things, no figurative explanation is needed; heaviness itself unambiguously means preponderance.

ELMALILI:101:6-7#2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:101:6-7#2/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:101:6-7#2/r1.claim: The heavy scales belong to those whose good deeds prevail.
ELMALILI:101:6-7#2/r1.anchor: Böyle mevâzîni ağır basan, güzel amelleri gālib gelen kimse

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:101:6/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:101:6/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:101:6/r1.claim: Mawazin may mean the things weighed, namely deeds; the translation prefers this reading.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:101:6/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:101:6/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:101:6/r2.claim: Alternatively, mawazin is the plural of mizan, “scales,” but metonymically still means the deeds weighed.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:101:6/r2.anchor: İkinci anlama göre de kelime kinaye olarak yine tartılan amelleri ifade eder

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:101:6/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:101:6/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:101:6/r3.claim: Heavy deeds signify an abundance of good that earns God's approval and eternal happiness in richly provisioned Gardens.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:101:6/r3.anchor: “Tartılan amellerin ağır gelmesi” hayır ve iyiliklerin fazla olmasını anlatmakta ve Allah’ın rızâsının bu sayede kazanılacağını göstermektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:101:6/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:101:6/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:101:6/r5.claim: Since afterlife events are unseen beyond what revelation states, one cannot speculate about how deeds will actually be weighed or measured.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:101:6/r5.anchor: amellerin nasıl tartılacağı veya ölçüleceği hakkında söz söylemek yahut fikir yürütmek ise mümkün değildir

QASHANI:101:1-5/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:101:1-5/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:101:1-5/r5.claim: This annihilation reading does not fit the later distinction of heavy and light scales; in God’s scale, rising and ascending count as weight, while descent is lightness: enduring righteous deeds matter most, and perishable pleasures have no weight.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p796/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p796/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p796/r6.claim: Mawazin may mean deeds with weight before God or weighing scales; heaviness is their being outweighed.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p796/r6.anchor: الموازين : جمع موزون وهو العمل الذي له وزن وخطر عند الله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p796/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p796/r7.speaker: أبو بكر
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p796/r7.claim: Abu Bakr told Umar that truth-followers' scales grow heavy through their conduct, while falsehood-followers' grow light; scales holding only good are rightly heavy.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p796/r7.anchor: ومنه حديث أبي بكر لعمر رضي الله عنهما في وصيته له : ( وإنما ثقلت موازين

TAB-FULL:v24p594#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p594#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p594#2/r2.claim: Al-Tabari explains that Arabic uses balance or weight for equivalence, citing an unnamed poet’s line about each disputant having a balance.
TAB-FULL:v24p594#2/r2.anchor: قال الشاعر: [البحر الكامل] قد كنت قبل لقائكم ذا مرة … عندي لكل مخاصم ميزانه

TAB-FULL:v24p594#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p594#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v24p594#2/r3.claim: Mujahid says there is no actual scale; the scale is a metaphor.
TAB-FULL:v24p594#2/r3.anchor: وكان مجاهد يقول: ليس ميزان، إنما هو مثل ضرب

TABATABAI:101:10-11/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:101:10-11/r7.speaker: القمي
TABATABAI:101:10-11/r7.claim: Al-Qummi glosses those whose scales are light as people with little good.
TABATABAI:101:10-11/r7.anchor: وفي قوله { وأما من خفت موازينه } قال من الحسنات

CORPUSCORANICUM:111:3-5:kommentar/r5.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:3-5:kommentar/r5.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:3-5:kommentar/r5.claim: Riddling that creates rhetorical tension also structures oath sequences such as Q 100 and teaching questions at 90:12–16, 97:2–4, 101:1–11, and 104:5–9.
CORPUSCORANICUM:111:3-5:kommentar/r5.anchor: auf dem Einsatz von Änigmatisierung zur Erzeugung rhetorischer Spannung basieren aber auch Schwurserien wie zu Beginn von Q 100

ABUHAYYAN:101:6/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:101:6/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:101:6/r1.claim: Abu Hayyan refers the discussion of the scales and their heaviness and lightness to al-Aʿraf.
ABUHAYYAN:101:6/r1.anchor: وتقدم الكلام في الموازين وثقلها وخفتها في الأعراف

ABUHAYYAN:101:6/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:101:6/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:101:6/r2.claim: The segment also refers the expression “a pleasing life” to Abu Hayyan's discussion of it in al-Haqqa.
ABUHAYYAN:101:6/r2.anchor: وتقدم الكلام في الموازين وثقلها وخفتها في الأعراف ، وعيشة راضية في الحاقة

ABUHAYYAN:101:7/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:101:7/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:101:7/r1.claim: Abu Hayyan again refers discussion of the scales and their heaviness and lightness to al-Aʿraf.
ABUHAYYAN:101:7/r1.anchor: وتقدم الكلام في الموازين وثقلها وخفتها في الأعراف

ALUSI:101:6/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:101:6/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:101:6/r1.claim: The passage summarizes the division of people into two groups and signals each group's particular state after describing what is common to all.
ALUSI:101:6/r1.anchor: بيان إجمالي لتحزب الناس حزبين وتنبيه على كيفية الأحوال الخاصة بكل منهما أثر بيان الأحوال الشاملة للكل

ALUSI:101:6/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:101:6/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI:101:6/r2.claim: The weighing of deeds is real and must be believed, though denying it does not make a person an unbeliever.
ALUSI:101:6/r2.anchor: وهذا إشارة إلى وزن الأعمال وهو مما يجب الايمان به حقيقة ولا يكفر منكره

ALUSI:101:6/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:101:6/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI:101:6/r3.claim: Weighing occurs after the records fly and are taken in the right or left hands, and after questioning and reckoning, as al-Wahidi and others state.
ALUSI:101:6/r3.anchor: ويكون بعد تطاير الصحف وأخذها بالايمان والشمائل وبعد السؤال والحساب كما ذكره الواحدي وغيره

ALUSI:101:6/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:101:6/r4.speaker: كنز الأسرار
ALUSI:101:6/r4.claim: Kanz al-Asrar describes a balance with a tongue and two pans, as broad as the heavens and earth, while its true nature is known to God.
ALUSI:101:6/r4.anchor: وجزم به صاحب كنز الأسرار بميزان له لسان وكفتان كإطباق السموات والأرض

ALUSI:101:6/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:101:6/r5.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن البصري
ALUSI:101:6/r5.claim: A tangible balance is transmitted from Ibn Abbas and al-Hasan al-Basri and attributed to many commentators by Sharh al-Maqasid.
ALUSI:101:6/r5.anchor: وقد روى القول به عن ابن عباس والحسن البصري

ALUSI:101:6/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:101:6/r6.speaker: نوادر الأصول
ALUSI:101:6/r6.claim: Nawadir al-Usul locates the balance between Paradise and Hell and describes its attachment to the Throne, with Gabriel holding its column and Michael overseeing it.
ALUSI:101:6/r6.anchor: ومكانه بين الجنة والنار كما في

ALUSI:101:6/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:101:6/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI:101:6/r7.claim: The best-known and sounder view is one balance for all communities and all deeds.
ALUSI:101:6/r7.anchor: والأشهر الأصح أنه ميزان واحد كما ذكرنا لجميع الأمم ولجميع الأعمال

ALUSI:101:6/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:101:6/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI:101:6/r8.claim: Mawāzīn is the plural of mīzān; its original wāw becomes yāʾ because it is quiescent after a kasra.
ALUSI:101:6/r8.anchor: وهو جمع ميزان وأصله موازن بالواو لكن قلبت ياء لسكونها وانكسار ما قبلها

ALUSI:101:6/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:101:6/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI:101:6/r9.claim: The plural may magnify the balance, as in the account of ʿAd denying the messengers.
ALUSI:101:6/r9.anchor: قيل للتعظيم كالجمع في قوله تعالى

ALUSI:101:6/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:101:6/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI:101:6/r10.claim: Alternatively, the plural may refer to the balance's parts, as in saying that someone's temples have gone gray.
ALUSI:101:6/r10.anchor: أو باعتبار أجزائه نحو شابت مفارقه

ALUSI:101:6/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:101:6/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI:101:6/r11.claim: A further explanation is multiple balances for distinct aspects; cited poetry speaks of flashes of lightning and rays of suns.
ALUSI:101:6/r11.anchor: أو باعتبار تعدد الأفراد للتغاير الاعتباري

ALUSI:101:6/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:101:6/r12.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI:101:6/r12.claim: Some say the deeds themselves are weighed: good deeds become beautiful luminous forms in the right pan and bad deeds ugly dark forms in the left, by God's grace and justice.
ALUSI:101:6/r12.anchor: وقال آخرون يوزن نفس الأعمال فتصور الصالحة بصور حسنة نوارنية ثم تطرح في كفة النور

ALUSI:101:6/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:101:6/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI:101:6/r13.claim: The objection that extraordinary transformations of realities are impossible is rejected, or limited to cases where the original reality's effects remain.
ALUSI:101:6/r13.anchor: وامتناع قلب الحقائق في مقام خرق العادات ممنوع أو مقيد ببقاء آثار الحقيقة الأولى

ALUSI:101:6/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:101:6/r14.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI:101:6/r14.claim: Others say God creates bodies corresponding to the deeds rather than transforming them, and claim a transmitted report supports this.
ALUSI:101:6/r14.anchor: وقد ذهب بعضهم إلى أن الله تعالى

ALUSI:101:6/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:101:6/r15.speaker: القرطبي
ALUSI:101:6/r15.claim: Al-Qurtubi says weight and lightness work as in this world: heavy deeds sink then rise to Illiyyin, while light ones flutter up then descend to Sijjin.
ALUSI:101:6/r15.anchor: والظاهر أن الثقل والخفة مثلهما في الدنيا فما ثقل نزل إلى أسفل ثم يرتفع إلى عليين

ALUSI:101:6/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:101:6/r16.speaker: بعض المتأخرين
ALUSI:101:6/r16.claim: A later scholar reverses the worldly mechanics: the believer's good deeds rise, while the unbeliever's pan becomes heavy because its other pan is empty; al-Alusi finds the cited verse inconclusive.
ALUSI:101:6/r16.anchor: وقال بعض المتأخرين هما على خلاف ما في الدنيا وإن عمل المؤمن إذا رجح صعد

ALUSI:101:6/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:101:6/r17.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI:101:6/r17.claim: One description weighs all deeds at once, with good deeds in the light pan at the right toward Paradise and bad deeds in the dark pan at the left toward Hell; God gives the person necessary knowledge of the result.
ALUSI:101:6/r17.anchor: وذكر بعضهم أن صفة الوزن أن يجعل جميع أعمال العباد في الميزان مرة واحدة الحسنات في كفة النور عن يمين العرش جهة الجنة

ALUSI:101:6/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:101:6/r18.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:101:6/r18.claim: Another account marks victory by a column of light rising from the good-deed pan and covering the bad-deed pan, and loss by a column of darkness; the four mechanics will be witnessed.
ALUSI:101:6/r18.anchor: وقيل نحوه إلا أن علامة الرجحان عمود من نور يثور من كفة الحسنات حتى يكسو كفة السيآت

ALUSI:101:6/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:101:6/r19.speaker: القرطبي
ALUSI:101:6/r19.claim: Al-Qurtubi says not everyone is weighed: a sound hadith exempts some of Muhammad's community from reckoning, and criminals recognized by their marks are seized by forelocks and feet; only those God wills remain to be weighed.
ALUSI:101:6/r19.anchor: قال القرطبي لا يكون في حق كل أحد لما في الحديث الصحيح فيقال يا محمد أدخل الجنة من أمتك من لا حساب عليهم

ALUSI:101:6/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:101:6/r20.speaker: منذر بن سعيد البلوطي
ALUSI:101:6/r20.claim: Qadi Mundhir ibn Saʿid al-Baluti says people of patience are not weighed; their reward is poured out for them.
ALUSI:101:6/r20.anchor: وذكر القاضي منذر بن سعيد البلوطي أن أهل الصبر لا توزن أعمالهم وإنما يصب لهم الأجر صباً

ALUSI:101:6/r21.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:101:6/r21.speaker: author
ALUSI:101:6/r21.claim: Al-Alusi says hypocrites apparently belong with unbelievers, but the truth is that their deeds are weighed too, given the many verses and hadiths.
ALUSI:101:6/r21.anchor: والظاهر أنه يدرج المنافق في الكافر والحق أن أعمالهم مطقلاً توزن لظواهر الآيات والأحاديث الكثيرة

ALUSI:101:6/r22.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:101:6/r22.speaker: author
ALUSI:101:6/r22.claim: Believing and unbelieving jinn are like humans in the weighing, and the two-party division here applies only among those whose deeds are weighed.
ALUSI:101:6/r22.anchor: والصحيح أن الجن مؤمنهم وكافرهم كالإنس في هذا الشأن

ALUSI:101:6/r23.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:101:6/r23.speaker: القرطبي
ALUSI:101:6/r23.claim: On al-Qurtubi's account, the passage divides those who are weighed into two groups rather than dividing every person without exception.
ALUSI:101:6/r23.anchor: والتقسيم فيما نحن فيه على ما سمعت عن القرطبي بالنسبة إلى من توزن أعماله لا بالنسبة إلى الناس مطلقاً

ALUSI:101:6/r24.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:101:6/r24.speaker: المعتزلة ومجاهد والضحاك والأعمش
ALUSI:101:6/r24.claim: The Muʿtazila and some Sunnis, including Mujahid, al-Dahhak, and al-Aʿmash, deny literal weighing: deeds are accidents, so weighing means equitable judgment and just decree.
ALUSI:101:6/r24.anchor: وأنكر المعتزلة الوزن حقيقة وجماعة من أهل السنة والجماعة منهم مجاهد والضحاك والأعمش قالوا إن الإعمال أعراض

ALUSI:101:6/r25.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:101:6/r25.speaker: الفراء
ALUSI:101:6/r25.claim: On the nonliteral view, mawāzīn may be plural of mawzūn, meaning deeds with weight and worth before God; heaviness means their measures and ranks prevail.
ALUSI:101:6/r25.anchor: وجوزوا فيما هنا أن تكون الموازين جمع موزون وهو العمل الذي له وزن وخطر عند الله تعالى

BAGHAWI:101:6/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:101:6/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:101:6/r1.claim: The one whose scales are heavy is the one whose good deeds outweigh the other deeds.
BAGHAWI:101:6/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى : { فأما من ثقلت موازينه } رجحت حسناته

BAYDAWI:101:6/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:101:6/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:101:6/r1.claim: His scales are heavy because the measures of the kinds of his good deeds outweigh.

BIQAI:101:6/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:101:6/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:101:6/r1.claim: Since a day is described by what happens in it, the discourse now distinguishes the people's outcomes.
BIQAI:101:6/r1.anchor: ولما كان اليوم إنما يوصف لأجل ما يقع فيه

BIQAI:101:6/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:101:6/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:101:6/r2.claim: The scales become heavy through outweighing.

BIQAI:101:6/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:101:6/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:101:6/r3.claim: The plural reflects the many kinds of good deeds done by following truth and avoiding falsehood; the weighed objects are deeds embodied and their records.
BIQAI:101:6/r3.anchor: ولما كانت الموزونات كثيرة الأنواع جداً

BIQAI:101:6/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:101:6/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI:101:6/r4.claim: The things weighed are both the deeds themselves, given bodily form, and their written records.

DURR:101:6/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:101:6/r3.speaker: قتادة
DURR:101:6/r3.claim: Qatada identifies the heavy-scale person's pleasing life as Paradise.
DURR:101:6/r3.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في قوله : { يوم يكون الناس كالفراش المبثوث }

DURR:101:8/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:101:8/r3.speaker: قتادة
DURR:101:8/r3.claim: Qatada identifies the heavy-scale person's pleasing life as Paradise.
DURR:101:8/r3.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في قوله : { يوم يكون الناس كالفراش المبثوث }

DURR:101:9/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:101:9/r3.speaker: قتادة
DURR:101:9/r3.claim: Qatada identifies the heavy-scale person's pleasing life as Paradise.
DURR:101:9/r3.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في قوله : { يوم يكون الناس كالفراش المبثوث }

IBNASHUR:101:6/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:101:6/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:101:6/r1.claim: This passage details the otherwise general picture of people spread like moths on that Day, dividing them into fortunate and wretched cases.
IBNASHUR:101:6/r1.anchor: من إجمال حال الناس حينئذ ، فذلك هو المقصود بذكر اسم الناس الشامل لأهل السعادة وأهل الشقاء

IBNASHUR:101:6/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:101:6/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:101:6/r2.claim: Heavy scales are a metonym for God's approval because weight entails substantial weighed goods, and Arabs use weight for merit, honor, and sound judgment.
IBNASHUR:101:6/r2.anchor: وثقل الموازين كناية عن كونه بمحل الرضى من الله تعالى لكثرة حسناته ، لأن ثقل الميزان يستلزم ثقل الموزون

IBNASHUR:101:6/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:101:6/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:101:6/r3.claim: The opposite idiom, that someone has no weight, means lacking merit; the Qur'an uses it of those given no weight on Judgment Day.
IBNASHUR:101:6/r3.anchor: وقد شاع عند العرب الكناية عن الفضل والشرف وأصالة الرأي بالوزن

IBNASHUR:101:6/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:101:6/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:101:6/r4.claim: The Arabic idiom already makes the weight's positive value clear, so the verse leaves unstated that righteous deeds are what make the scales heavy.
IBNASHUR:101:6/r4.anchor: فلذلك لم يصرح في الآية بذكر ما يُثقل الموازين لظهور أنه العمل الصالح

IBNASHUR:101:6/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:101:6/r5.speaker: ابن العربي
IBNASHUR:101:6/r5.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabi says no sound hadith establishes the scale; the point is that no deed is lost, and God can accomplish this with an instrument, angels, or another means.
IBNASHUR:101:6/r5.anchor: قال ابن العربي في « العواصم » : لم يرد حديث صحيح في الميزان . والمقصودُ عدم فوات شيء من الأعمال

IBNATIYYA:101:6/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:101:6/r1.speaker: جمهور العلماء والفقهاء والمحدثين
IBNATIYYA:101:6/r1.claim: Most scholars, jurists, and hadith scholars affirm a literal balance on the Resurrection, with a beam, so people can understand divine judgment through a form they know and trust.
IBNATIYYA:101:6/r1.anchor: فقال جمهور العلماء والفقهاء والمحدثين : ميزان القيامة بعمود

IBNATIYYA:101:6/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:101:6/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA:101:6/r2.claim: Mujāhid denies a literal balance and takes it as a metaphor for justice, since a scale is the fairest measure known to people.
IBNATIYYA:101:6/r2.anchor: وقال مجاهد : ليس تم ميزان ؛ إنما هو العدل ، مثل ذكره بالميزان ؛ إذ هو أعدل ما يدري الناس

IBNATIYYA:101:6/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:101:6/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:101:6/r3.claim: The plural balances are assigned to a person because that person has many different things to be weighed.
IBNATIYYA:101:6/r3.anchor: وجمعت الموازين للإنسان لما كانت له موزونات كثيرة متغايرة

IBNATIYYA:101:6/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:101:6/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:101:6/r4.claim: A balance is heavy through faith and deeds, and light through their absence or scarcity; a believer’s balance will never be disastrously light.
IBNATIYYA:101:6/r4.anchor: وثقل هذا الميزان هو بالإيمان والأعمال ، وخفته بعدمها وقلتها ، ولن يخف خفة موبقة ميزان مؤمن

IBNKATHIR:101:6/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:101:6/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:101:6/r1.claim: People's deeds lead to honor or humiliation according to what they did; heavy scales mean their good deeds outweigh their bad deeds.
IBNKATHIR:101:6/r1.anchor: أخبر تعالى عما يئول إليه عمل العاملين ، وما يصيرون إليه من الكرامة أو الإهانة

MAWARDI:101:6/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:101:6/r1.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI:101:6/r1.claim: Al-Hasan says the balances are two-pan scales weighing good and evil deeds.
MAWARDI:101:6/r1.anchor: أحدها : أنه ميزان ذو كفتين توزن به الحسنات والسيئات ،   قاله الحسن

MAWARDI:101:6/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:101:6/r2.speaker: أبو بكر
MAWARDI:101:6/r2.claim: Abu Bakr remarks that a scale into which only truth is placed rightly weighs heavily.
MAWARDI:101:6/r2.anchor: قال أبو بكر رضي الله عنه : وحق لميزان لا يوضع فيه إلا الحق أن يكون ثقيلاً .

MAWARDI:101:6/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:101:6/r3.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI:101:6/r3.claim: Mujahid says the balances mean reckoning; the saying that a person's tongue is his weight and a poet's balance for each disputant (his answering speech) illustrate the sense.
MAWARDI:101:6/r3.anchor:
الثاني : الميزان هو الحساب ،   قاله مجاهد ،   ولذلك قيل : اللسان وزن الإنسان ،   وقال الشاعر :
قد كنت قبل لقائكم ذا مرةٍ *** عندي لكل مخاصم ميزانه

MAWARDI:101:6/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:101:6/r4.speaker: عبد العزيز بن يحيى
MAWARDI:101:6/r4.claim: ʿAbd al-ʿAziz ibn Yahya says the balances are arguments and proofs, citing the preceding poem.
MAWARDI:101:6/r4.anchor: الثالث : أن الموازين الحجج والدلائل ،   قاله عبد العزيز بن يحيى ،   واستشهد فيه بالشعر المتقدم .

MAWARDI:101:6/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:101:6/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI:101:6/r5.claim: Mawazin can be the plural of mizan (scale) or of mawzun (that which is weighed).
MAWARDI:101:6/r5.anchor: وفي الموازين وجهان : أحدهما : جمع ميزان . الثاني : أنه جمع موزون .

NASAFI:101:6/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:101:6/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:101:6/r1.claim: The scales weigh heavily because their owners followed the truth.
NASAFI:101:6/r1.anchor: { فَأَمَّا مَن ثَقُلَتْ موازينه } باتباعهم الحق

NASAFI:101:6/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:101:6/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI:101:6/r2.claim: Mawazin may be the plural of mawzun, a deed with weight and standing before God, or the plural of mizan, with heaviness meaning that the scale tips in one's favor.
NASAFI:101:6/r2.anchor: وهي جمع موزون ،   وهو العمل الذي له وزن وخطر عند الله ،   أو جمع ميزان وثقلها رجحانها .

RAZI:101:6/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:101:6/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:101:6/r1.claim: On describing the Resurrection, God divides people into two groups according to the heaviness or lightness of their scales.
RAZI:101:6/r1.anchor: لما وصف يوم القيامة قسم الناس فيه إلى قسمين

RAZI:101:6/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:101:6/r2.speaker: الفراء
RAZI:101:6/r2.claim: Al-Farrāʾ takes mawāzīn as the plural of mawzūn, meaning a deed with weight and worth before God; he compares it to saying one thing is by the measure or weight of another.
RAZI:101:6/r2.anchor: وهذا قول الفراء قال : ونظيره يقال : عندي درهم بميزان درهمك ووزن درهمك

RAZI:101:6/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:101:6/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI:101:6/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās takes the word as balances with a tongue and two pans: obedient people's good deeds appear beautiful and, if they outweigh, lead to Paradise; unbelievers' evil deeds appear ugly and light, leading to the Fire.
RAZI:101:6/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس : الميزان له لسان وكفتان لا يوزن فيه إلا الأعمال فيؤتى بحسنات المطيع في أحسن صورة

RAZI:101:6/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:101:6/r4.speaker: الحسن
RAZI:101:6/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the balance has two pans but does not describe it further.
RAZI:101:6/r4.anchor: وقال الحسن : في الميزان له كفتان ولا يوصف

RAZI:101:6/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:101:6/r5.speaker: المتكلمون
RAZI:101:6/r5.claim: The theologians say deeds themselves cannot be weighed, especially after ceasing to exist; instead, records may be weighed, light and darkness may signify good and evil, or the records may be embodied beautifully or hideously, publicly revealing people's standing.
RAZI:101:6/r5.anchor: قال المتكلمون : إن نفس الحسنات والسيئات لا يصح وزنهما

BURHAN:v4p317/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p317/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p317/r6.claim: Its overt complement may be a definite plural, generic noun, pronoun, or indefinite singular.
BURHAN:v4p317/r6.anchor: ويضاف تارة إلى الجمع المعرف نحو

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p225/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p225/r9.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p225/r9.claim: A fifth sense is weight or predominance, as in the weighing scales on the Last Day.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p225/r9.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن الثقل في القرآن على عشرة أوجه
